name: saranga
description: SARANGA (Structured ArXiv Representation, Automatic Network Generation and Analysis): a mid-level representation of mathematical knowledge extracted from ~100,000 arXiv papers across 20 subject categories in mathematics, computer science, and statistics. Each paper is represented as a typed directed acyclic graph where nodes are mathematical objects (definitions, theorems, lemmas, propositions, corollaries, conjectures, claims, problems, open problems, proofs, algorithms, assumptions, examples, exercises, remarks) with assumption/conclusion splits, raw LaTeX, cleaned text, and cross-references, and edges are typed dependencies (uses, generalizes, specializes, proves, illustrates, tests). The dataset includes per-paper extracted graphs, cross-paper alignments, and a foundation knowledge graph of ~298K mathematical objects integrated from formal-logic libraries, natural-language theorem collections, and encyclopedic references. Extracted using a purely rule-based parser that requires no LLM calls at inference time.
cr:citeAs: Anonymous (2026). Saranga: Structured Mathematical Knowledge Extraction at Scale via Neural-to-Rule Ensemble Distillation.

prov:wasGeneratedBy: Papers sourced from arXiv bulk data across 20 subject categories (math.CO, math.AG, math.AP, math.AT, math.CA, math.DG, math.FA, math.GR, math.LO, math.NA, math.NT, math.OC, math.PR, math.RT, math-ph, cs.CC, cs.DS, cs.IT, cs.LG, stat.TH). LaTeX source files parsed programmatically using the Authomathics rule-based parser with NtRED-distilled rules. Extraction is fully automated with no human annotation.
rai:dataCollectionType: Automated extraction from publicly available arXiv LaTeX sources. Papers were sampled from 20 arXiv categories spanning pure mathematics, applied mathematics, theoretical computer science, and statistics.
rai:dataLimitations: The parser is rule-based and may miss non-standard LaTeX environments or custom theorem styles not covered by the distilled rules. Assumption/conclusion splitting relies on linguistic heuristics and may be imprecise for complex mathematical phrasing. Papers that use PDF-only submissions (no LaTeX source) are excluded. Some categories have fewer papers due to availability constraints.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset reflects the conventions and topics of arXiv papers in the selected categories. Coverage skews toward active research areas with higher submission rates (e.g., math.CO, cs.LG). English-language papers only. Author demographics and institutional representation are not balanced.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information. The dataset contains only mathematical content extracted from publicly available arXiv papers. Author names appear only as part of theorem attributions within the mathematical text (e.g., 'Ramsey's Theorem').
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for: (1) evaluating mathematical structure extraction systems, (2) training/fine-tuning models for mathematical information extraction, (3) constructing cross-paper mathematical knowledge graphs, (4) studying the structure and conventions of mathematical writing across subfields, (5) benchmarking graph alignment and anomaly detection on mathematical corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: enables large-scale computational study of mathematical literature, supports open science, and provides a reusable resource for the mathematical AI community. Negative risks are minimal as the data is purely mathematical content from public sources with no privacy concerns.
rai:dataCollection: Source documents are arXiv preprints downloaded as LaTeX source via the public arXiv API, drawn at 500 papers per (category, year) over 2010-2019 across 20 mathematical and theoretical-CS categories (seed 42; cross-listed papers excluded). Foundation-graph entries are imported programmatically from Mathlib (Lean 4) via LeanDojo, Herald (NL translations of Mathlib theorems), NaturalProofs (ProofWiki + the Stacks Project), and three encyclopedic reference books used under fair-use index extraction. T1 hand-gold papers were selected by the authors as a small evaluation sample spanning paradigmatic mathematical writing styles.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: LaTeX is parsed into a typed DAG of mathematical nodes (definitions, theorems, proofs, etc.) with typed dependency edges. Three production extractors operate at distinct quality-scale trade-offs: T1 hand-annotation, T2 LLM extraction (Claude Opus with per-node-type prompts), and T3 deterministic regex-over-LaTeX whose rules were refined via the Neural-to-Rule Ensemble Distillation (NtRED) procedure documented in the paper. Equations inside proofs are stored either as Level-1 sibling nodes (T3 v1.0) or as Level-2 sub-nodes of the parent proof (T2 default). Nodes are linked to the foundation graph via Aho-Corasick multi-pattern matching with IDF stop-word filtering.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: T1 (10 papers): hand-annotated by a single annotator following the typed-DAG schema documented in Section 3 and Appendix A of the paper. Two case-study golds (Candes-Tao, Sinkhorn) are iteratively curated against silver Opus extractions and kept out of the headline evaluation set. T2 (250 papers): extracted by Claude Opus 4.6 with structure-type-specific prompts that encode the type-promotion rule, origin attribution, and assumption/conclusion separation; the prompts are released in the code repository. T3 (~98K papers): generated by a deterministic Python regex pipeline whose rules were iteratively refined against T1 gold via NtRED. Inter-annotator agreement is not yet reported (single annotator T1 v1.0); planned for v1.1.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: v1.0 released with the NeurIPS 2026 E&D submission. v1.1 with rule-based extractor improvements (name-field population, single-environment proof preservation, equation grouping into parent proofs) is planned within 1-2 months of submission. Long-term hosting on HuggingFace Datasets; the dataset URL is versioned via the standard HF revision system, so v1.0 remains accessible at a frozen revision URL even as later versions are released. Reported numerical results are pinned to v1.0 for reproducibility; v1.1 will ship updated baselines on the same benchmark protocol.
rai:hasSyntheticData: No. All content is extracted from real human-authored arXiv papers. The extraction process is deterministic (rule-based with NtRED-distilled rules), but the underlying mathematical content is not synthetic or generated.
